items.title: Ollama SSRF via unvalidated blob-pull redirects (CVE-2026-85180) — unpatched
items.text:
*CRITICAL* — Ollama SSRF via unvalidated blob-pull redirects (CVE-2026-85180)
Ollama does not validate redirect destinations when pulling tensor-layer model blobs, letting a malicious or compromised registry redirect the download to an arbitrary host — including cloud metadata endpoints (169.254.169.254). CVSS 8.7 (High). Published 2026-09-03. No patched version available yet.
CardiTrack's MedGemma image (`src/Infrastructure/MedGemma/Dockerfile`) is `FROM ollama/ollama:latest` (unpinned) and pulls the model from a third-party HuggingFace mirror (`hf.co/unsloth/medgemma-1.5-4b-it-GGUF`) via `ollama pull` at build time — exactly the code path this advisory describes.
https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-57p7-34ff-7w3w

claude "work through @research/queue/2026-09-19-ollama-ssrf-blob-pull-redirect.md"

items.title: Ollama GGUF decoder integer overflow (CVE-2026-86289) — patched in 0.31.2-rc1
items.text:
*HIGH* — Ollama GGUF decoder integer overflow (CVE-2026-86289), patched
Integer overflow in Ollama's GGUF string-reading code (`readGGUFV1String`), remotely triggerable while loading a model file. CVSS 2.1 (Low), but it's in the exact GGUF-parsing path used to load the unsloth MedGemma artifact. Published 2026-09-07, fixed in Ollama 0.31.2-rc1.
CardiTrack's MedGemma base image is unpinned (`ollama/ollama:latest`), so whether the running image carries the fix depends entirely on build date.
https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-c2q9-58w2-gjg4

claude "work through @research/queue/2026-09-19-ollama-gguf-decoder-integer-overflow.md"

items.title: Terraform google/google-beta provider v8.0.0 GA drops several resource families with no deprecation grace
items.text:
*FYI* — Terraform google/google-beta provider hits v8.0.0 GA, drops resources with no deprecation grace
`hashicorp/google` and `hashicorp/google-beta` went GA on v8.0.0 (~2026-09-03) and are iterating fast (v8.4.0 by 09-18). v8 removes `google_beyondcorp_app_connection/connector/gateway`, `google_iap_brand`/`google_iap_client`, `google_ml_engine_model`, and all `google_notebooks_*` resources — outright, not deprecated-then-removed.
CardiTrack's `versions.tf` pins `~>7.23`, so nothing breaks today. Worth confirming none of `infrastructure/**` uses those four resource families before anyone widens the constraint.
https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform-provider-google/releases

claude "work through @research/queue/2026-09-19-terraform-google-provider-v8-ga.md"

items.title: Google Health API v4 adds read-only Women's Health scopes (logged symptoms, mindfulness, reproductive health)
items.text:
*FYI* — Google Health API v4 adds read-only Women's Health scopes
The discovery document gained three new read-only scopes (`googlehealth.logged_symptoms.readonly`, `.mindfulness.readonly`, `.reproductive_health.readonly`), the read-half of the write-only Women's Health types shipped 2026-08-17. Purely additive — existing scopes and payload shapes are unchanged.
No action needed unless CardiTrack wants to ingest these new data types.
https://developers.google.com/health/release-notes

claude "work through @research/queue/2026-09-19-google-health-api-womens-health-read-scopes.md"

items.title: Garmin Connect Developer Program's public application form removed — no ETA
items.text:
*HIGH* — Garmin Connect Developer Program's application form removed, no ETA
Garmin froze new developer applications in spring 2026 (after a Strava API-terms lawsuit) and has now removed the public application form from developer.garmin.com entirely — "Stay tuned for more updates," no ETA. Existing integrations and Connect IQ are unaffected, but that's not CardiTrack's path.
CardiTrack's `garmin` provider is a config-only stub awaiting developer-program access for planned R2 engine work; the docs already named Withings as the fallback if access didn't come — this closes that path indefinitely rather than merely gating it.
https://the5krunner.com/2026/09/14/garmin-developer-api-access-paused/

claude "work through @research/queue/2026-09-19-garmin-connect-developer-program-closed.md"

items.title: UK National Commission into the Regulation of AI in Healthcare publishes final recommendations
items.text:
*HIGH* — UK National Commission into the Regulation of AI in Healthcare publishes final recommendations
An MHRA-convened independent commission (NHS-doctor-chaired, 12,000+ respondents) published its final report on 2026-09-10: continuous real-world post-market monitoring for AI-enabled medical devices, oversight proportionate to patient risk rather than a fixed device/non-device binary, a public incident database, and a "patients should know when AI is used in their care" transparency expectation.
Not yet law — no dated compliance obligation — but the risk-proportionate framing is exactly the kind of test that could eventually decide whether CardiTrack's narration tool sits inside SaMD scope, and the transparency recommendation is worth checking against CardiTrack's existing AI-disclosure copy.
https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/national-commission-into-the-regulation-of-ai-in-healthcare-recommendations-for-a-future-regulatory-framework

claude "work through @research/queue/2026-09-19-uk-ai-healthcare-commission-recommendations.md"
